How to recover from burnout
without quitting your life
Admit it out loud. Tell your partner, a friend or your manager that you're running on empty. Hiding it only makes the hole deeper and the recovery longer.
Protect your sleep first. Fixed bedtime, no screens late, a dark room. Nothing heals a tired mind faster than a few weeks of real, regular sleep.
Cut what isn't essential. Extra projects, social obligations, side tasks. Keep the few things that truly matter and drop the rest for a while.
Move gently every day. A walk outside, an easy swim, light stretching. Calm movement lowers stress without draining the little energy you have left.
Fill your mind with something light. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives my brain a rest from work and worries.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives my brain a rest from work and worries.

slides.texte_overlay: Schedule real breaks in your day. Ten minutes away from the desk every two hours. Small pauses stop the tiredness from building up again.
Talk to a professional if it lasts. A doctor or a therapist can help you recover faster. Asking for help is a smart move, not a weakness.
